page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-32-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for high-throughput, latency-sensitive database architectures and high-density data processing. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration is powered by dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processors supplying 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The CPU includes 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced acceleration features including Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets, enabling hardware-level optimization for cryptographic, matrix math, and vector computation workloads without discrete accelerator hardware.

The instance pairs its 32 vCPUs with 256 GB of system RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio characteristic of memory-rich deployments. A primary differentiator is its bundled high-density storage subsystem, comprising 12,884 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage across four drives. Synthetic and application testing reveals solid aggregate performance across general computation, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching 14,066 and PassMark CPU overall scoring 37,463.33. Memory subsystem evaluations demonstrate sustained throughput, recording 115.28 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 49.39 GB/sec in large-block writes. The CPU instruction set enables strong throughput on lightweight deep learning inference tasks, exceeding 2,433 tokens per second on 135M parameter prompt processing and 321 tokens per second on text generation. Redis key-value operations achieve 35.61 million operations per second.

Qualitatively, z3-highmem-32-highlssd optimizes cost efficiency by bundling massive high-speed NVMe storage directly within the instance, avoiding separate network-attached disk volume provisioning and IOPS reservation overheads. However, architectural tradeoffs include the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe storage, requiring application-level data replication strategies to manage instance lifecycle events. Additionally, this instance provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses and lacks discrete GPUs, restricting its utility for heavy graphics processing or massive multi-billion parameter model training. The server is ideally configured for operational databases, large distributed NoSQL engines, in-memory caching with persistent snapshots, and real-time analytical indexing.
description: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-32-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads requiring dense local storage and high memory capacity. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processors featuring a 105 MB L3 cache and advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. It includes 256 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, alongside 12,884 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across four bundled drives. Benchmark results show balanced multi-core computing capability alongside strong image processing and lightweight LLM inference throughput, achieving over 2,400 tokens per second on prompt processing for compact models. With 35.61 million operations per second in Redis benchmarks, the instance delivers predictable performance for storage-heavy architectures. The server fits high-throughput transactional databases, large NoSQL datastores, distributed caching layers, and search indexers needing low-latency direct-attached storage without dedicated accelerator hardware.
